title: SpinBench: Perspective and Rotation as a Lens on Spatial Reasoning in VLMs
claim: A benchmark is organized into progressively structured task groups, each shown with representative example questions covering distinct facets of one capability.
layout: 7 rounded cards in a 3-row mosaic; colored headers; stats column at left
description: A mosaic of seven rounded, color-coded cards, one per task group of the benchmark. The top row holds Identity matching (red), Dynamic rotation (yellow) and Dynamic translation (purple). The middle row holds Object-relation grounding (green), with pink and blue highlights marking seed questions and symmetrical and syntactic augmentations. The bottom row holds Mental rotation (red), Canonical view selection (teal) and a large Perspective taking card (blue). Perspective taking has sub-panels for Scene Selection, Relation Transformation and Relation Transformation with premise. Each card gives short example questions with answer options and the correct answer underlined in green. Real photos sit beside the questions: cars, chairs, faces, tabletop objects and furniture. A vertical rainbow 'SpinBench' logo and summary stats (7 groups, 51 tasks, 2739 samples) sit at the left.
caption: Overview of SpinBench task design across seven task groups. Representative subtasks are illustrated for each group with simplified question wording for clarity. In the released benchmark, all queries include explicit frame-of-reference definitions to avoid ambiguity. Human face data are sourced from the Stereo Face Database [ref] and are licensed for research use only.
abstract: We present SpinBench, a cognitively grounded diagnostic benchmark for evaluating spatial reasoning in vision language models (VLMs). SpinBench is designed around the core challenge of spatial reasoning: perspective taking, the ability to reason about how scenes and object relations change under viewpoint transformation. Since perspective taking requires multiple cognitive capabilities, such as recognizing objects across views, relative positions grounding, and mentally simulating transformations, SpinBench introduces a set of fine-grained diagnostic categories. Our categories target translation, rotation, object relative pose, and viewpoint change, and are progressively structured so that single-object simpler tasks scaffold toward the most demanding multi-object perspective-taking setting. We evaluate 43 state-of-the-art VLMs, both proprietary and open source. Results reveal systematic weaknesses: strong egocentric bias, poor rotational understanding, and inconsistencies under symmetrical and syntactic reformulations. Scaling analysis shows both smooth improvements and emergent capabilities. While human subjects achieve high accuracy (91.2\%), task difficulty as measured by human response time shows strong correlation with VLM accuracy, indicating that SpinBench captures spatial reasoning challenges shared across humans and VLMs. We believe SpinBench provides critical insights into spatial reasoning in VLMs and highlights key gaps in their ability to reason about physical space. Our website can be found at https://spinbench25.github.io/.
